linkages: We link data across sources and family members using a unique personal identifier (children to parents, siblings and grandparents).
Focal children are linked to older (female) siblings and to mothers for the spillover analyses.

sample.universe: The universe of births in Denmark between 1997 and 2019, with vaccine adherence measured up to and including the outcome year 2021; the public childhood vaccination program covers all resident children between the ages of three months and 12 years
sample.unit_of_observation: child (individual), with family members linked for the spillover analyses
selection_rules: 2014 reform: three separate samples of children turning 2, 6.5 and 14 within 100 days around the 15 May 2014 implementation date
2017 reform: three samples of children turning 2, 6.5 and 14 in the 100 days prior to and past the 6 February 2017 introduction date for digital reminders

2019 reform: three separate samples of children who are born, turn four and turn 12 in the 60 days prior to and after the relevant cut-off dates (1 August 2019 for the first-year vaccination sample; 1 November 2019 for the MMR booster and HPV samples)
The 60-day rather than 100-day bandwidth for 2019 is imposed by GP expenses data ending in 2021, so that outcomes are observed for all children in the sample
The main HPV analyses are based on (eligible) female children only; the gender comparison in Fig. 7 adds male children, who became eligible in July 2019
sample.period: 2014-2021 (reform samples around the 2014, 2017 and 2019 cut-offs; outcomes through 2021)
sample.n_observations: 2014 reform: 43,203 control and 43,440 treatment children; 2017 reform: 40,967 and 42,044; 2019 reform: 26,661 and 25,819 (Table 2, combining the age-specific samples of each reform)

construction_notes: Outcomes are indicators for having received the relevant vaccination by a given age, constructed from individual-level GP reimbursement records; the reimbursement data contain the week of service rather than the actual day (footnote 20).

Vaccination coverage is measured one year after dispatch of the reminder for the 2014 and 2017 reforms (coverage at ages 3, 7.5 and 15) and at age 2y3mo / 6y1mo / 14y1mo for the 2019 reform, which also allows a comparison one year after the recommended vaccination age.
Income of mothers and fathers in Table 2 is in 1000 DKK; background characteristics are measured one year prior to the reforms.
Health education is an indicator for at least one parent having completed training as a medical doctor, midwife, early childhood teacher or nurse.
GP expenses used as a spillover outcome exclude vaccinations and preventive health checks.
Validation studies cited in footnote 10 find under-reporting of vaccinations in the 2-5 percentage point range; the authors argue reporting should not depend on treatment assignment.

claims.statement: Prospective HPV reminders sent in 2019 for a child did not increase the probability that the child's mother took up cervical cancer screening in the following year.

treatment.label: Introduction of prospective reminder letters, 2019 reform (HPV sample, 1 November 2019 cut-off at age 12)

register_source.value: Statistics Denmark administrative data (child's date of birth, which determines treatment assignment)

definition.value: Indicator for turning 12 years of age on or after 1 November 2019 and hence being enrolled in the new prospective reminder policy for all future vaccinations (reminder two weeks before the recommended vaccination age plus a follow-up reminder one month after if non-compliant); children turning 12 earlier would, if non-adherent, receive a retrospective reminder letter at age 14.

timing.value: Assigned by date of birth; reminders are sent two weeks prior to each recommended vaccination age, with a follow-up reminder one month after the recommended age.

outcome.label: Cervical cancer screening for mothers of children in the HPV sample

register_source.value: Statistics Denmark: GP reimbursement data (cervical cancer screenings for mothers), linked across family members by a unique personal identifier

definition.value: Probability of mothers of focal children receiving a cervical cancer screening within a year following the age of dispatch of the HPV reminder; the triennial screening is offered to every woman between 23 and 59 years.

timing.value: Within a year following the age of dispatch of the HPV reminder

units.value: share of mothers screened within the year

magnitude.interpretation: About 15 percent of mothers have a screening in that period and we find no evidence of a discontinuity at the cut-off.

estimand.target_population: Mothers of children turning 12 around the 1 November 2019 cut-off
estimand.compliers: Not an instrumental-variables design: treatment is assigned sharply by date of birth, so the estimate is local to children reaching the relevant age just around the 2019 cut-off. All treated parents receive the prospective reminder, so the estimate is an intention-to-treat effect of the reminder regime relative to the retrospective-reminder control regime.
estimand.time_horizon: Within a year following the age of dispatch of the HPV reminder
estimand.formal_query: E[y | do(2019 prospective reminder regime)] - E[y | do(2017 retrospective digital reminder regime)] for children at the cut-off

population.description: Mothers of the focal children in the 2019 HPV sample (the triennial cervical cancer screening is offered to every woman between 23 and 59 years)
population.ages: Mothers of 12-year-olds; screening offered to women aged 23-59
population.selection: Mothers linked to a focal child in the 60-day RD window around the 1 November 2019 cut-off

identification.source_of_variation: The 1 August 2019 (date of birth) and 1 November 2019 (turning four and turning 12) cut-offs for enrolment into the new prospective reminder policy; control children remained under the 2017 retrospective digital reminder rules.

key_assumptions.assumption: Parents cannot select into treatment: the running variable (the child's date of birth, and hence the date at which the child reaches the relevant age) cannot be manipulated around the reform cut-off.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Graphical 2-day binned histograms of the running variable (Appendix Figures A4-A6) and a formal McCrary (2008) density test (Appendix Table A7); the test cannot reject no bunching in the 2014 and 2019 samples but indicates bunching in two of the 2017 samples (10 percent level).

key_assumptions.assumption: Continuity/smoothness at the cut-off: potential outcomes and other pre-treatment characteristics develop smoothly in the running variable around the cut-off, so the left-hand limit identifies the counterfactual mean for the treated at the cut-off.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Balance of parental background characteristics in Table 2 and tests for discontinuities in pre-birth parental characteristics at the cut-offs (Appendix Tables A8-A10), which show no systematic discontinuities.

key_assumptions.assumption: Exclusion: date of birth relative to the cut-off affects the outcome only through assignment to the reminder regime, i.e. nothing else changes discontinuously at the cut-off date.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The reforms were implemented nationally on fixed dates and assignment is 'exclusively determined by children's date of birth'; no other policy change at the same cut-off is discussed.

implies_edges.to: Cervical cancer screening for mothers of children in the HPV sample

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimated effect of the 2019 reform bundles the change in reminder timing (prospective rather than retrospective) and the simultaneous change in reminder content (messages on positive externalities and social desirability); the two cannot be separated.

threats_discussed: Manipulation/bunching of the running variable around the cut-offs (McCrary test cannot reject no bunching in the 2019 samples)
Simultaneity of the change in reminder timing and the change in reminder content
Short follow-up (outcome data only through 2021), which forces a 60-day bandwidth and rules out some vaccinations
Low power for longer-run spillover outcomes
robustness_checks: Specification curves over seven bandwidths and five estimation methods, Appendix Figure A3
Calonico et al. (2020) optimal-bandwidth estimates reported alongside the 60-day bandwidth in Table 4 (0.024, 0.050** and 0.034 for columns 1-3)
Placebo analyses using the RD-DD control samples at the respective cut-off dates in the year before, which show no significant jumps (results available on request)
McCrary (2008) density test (Appendix Table A7) and balance tests on pre-birth parental characteristics
unresolved_confounders: The change in reminder timing and the change in reminder content were implemented simultaneously and at scale, so their separate contributions cannot be disentangled
